newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close strong at new high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close strong at new high.

text.p: CME live cattle futures rebounded from early profit taking to post another new contract high in April late on expectations of further gains in cash cattle next week, traders said.

Live cattle finished 0.550 to 0.100 cent higher with April up most at 69.250 cents after posting a new high of 69.300 late. February expired earlier, up 0.500 at 68.100, after setting a new high of 68.250. October also set a new high of 68.200 cents.
Expectations that cash cattle markets will continue to rise next week kept futures supported, they said.
"They (packers) are going to have to pay up (for cattle) next week," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.
The firming beef market and tighter feedlot showlists could prompt packers to pay $67 per cwt sometime next week, traders added.
R.J. O'Brien and LIT division of First Options bought late while RBH sold, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses sold June 68 and 70 calls and there was short covering in April 68 and 70 calls. Volatility was steady, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures ended 0.075 cent higher to 0.300 lower with only March up at 68.275 cents.
Feeders found some spillover support from live cattle, but were generally pressured by higher corn futures and profit taking on an overbought condition, traders said.
LIT spread long May/short March late to offset some of the spillover buying from live cattle. ADM Investor Services bought March 68 calls early, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.04 at $68.88 per cwt.
